name: Tomato Catsup
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: eight quarts or one peck of tomatas
ingredients.originalText: eight quarts or one peck of tomatas
ingredients.quantityText: eight quarts or one peck of tomatas

instructions.text: Put tomatas into a tub in layers about two inches in thickness, sprinkling a handful of salt between each layer
Cover the tub and let it set for three days
Early in the morning, put the tomatas into a large porcelain kettle, and boil it slowly and steadily till ten at night, frequently mashing and stirring the tomatas
Next morning strain and press it through a sieve
Put it into a clean kettle with two ounces of cloves, one ounce of mace, two ounces of black pepper, and two table-spoonfuls of cayenne, all powdered
Let it boil slowly and steadily all day, and put it to cool in the evening in a large pan
Cover it, and let it set all night
Next day put it into small bottles, securing the corks by dipping them in melted rosin, and tying leathers over them

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Put tomatas into a tub in layers about two inches in thickness, sprinkling a handful of salt between each layer
2. Cover the tub and let it set for three days
3. Early in the morning, put the tomatas into a large porcelain kettle, and boil it slowly and steadily till ten at night, frequently mashing and stirring the tomatas
4. Put it out to cool
5. Next morning strain and press it through a sieve
6. Put it into a clean kettle with two ounces of cloves, one ounce of mace, two ounces of black pepper, and two table-spoonfuls of cayenne, all powdered
7. Let it boil slowly and steadily all day, and put it to cool in the evening in a large pan
8. Cover it, and let it set all night
9. Next day put it into small bottles, securing the corks by dipping them in melted rosin, and tying leathers over them
